findings.title: 28 ghost skill registrations in skill-rules.json (26 arscontexta-* from removed plugin + 2 archived skills) with live triggers — hook injects 'SKILL ACTIVATION CHECK' for skills that don't exist
findings.observe_how: Diff Object.keys(rules.skills) against `ls .claude/skills/`: 26 arscontexta-* entries plus idearalph and environment-triage have no skill directory anywhere in the repo (idearalph and environment-triage exist only in .claude/skills/.archive/; no arscontexta dir exists in repo or ~/.claude/skills — the runtime available-skills list confirms none are loaded). skill-activation-prompt.ts has no existsSync check on the suggested skill (only on the rules file and pattern script, lines 180/342/344). The 28 ghosts carry ~85 live keywords + 30 intentPatterns: environment-triage matches everyday dev prompts ('pip install', 'import error', 'venv', 'ModuleNotFoundError'); arscontexta-learn matches 'learn about'; arscontexta-remember's '/remember' keyword shadows the REAL remember skill, which has no registration at all. Matching prompts inject a SKILL ACTIVATION CHECK telling the model to activate a nonexistent skill. Five test files (.claude/hooks/src/__tests__/arscontexta-*.test.ts) actively pin the dead entries, adding maintenance weight. Fix: deregister the 28 entries (and decide whether the arscontexta test suite should die with them); add a dir-existence filter in the hook as defense-in-depth.
findings.telemetry: Count of skill-activation suggestions naming a skill absent from .claude/skills/ per week (expected to drop to 0 after deregistration); secondary: Skill-tool invocation failures for arscontexta-*/environment-triage/idearalph.

findings.title: railway-cli and neonctl registered as top-level JSON keys outside the skills map, in a non-schema shape — registrations are dead despite status 'verified'
findings.observe_how: skill-rules.json top-level keys are [version, description, skills, agents, patterns, notes, railway-cli, neonctl] — the last two sit AFTER the notes block (lines 2909 and 2922), outside skills{}. They also use a flat {keywords, score, status} shape with no promptTriggers wrapper, so even if moved under skills they would be skipped by the hook's `if (!triggers) continue` (line 401). Net effect: zero prompt-trigger routing for two actively-documented CLI skills (both have rules: railway-deploy.md, neonctl-safety.md) while the registry claims status 'verified' / score 90 — a false routing claim that would survive any audit reading only the status fields. Fix: move both under skills{} in the promptTriggers schema; find and fix the registrar/vetting step that appended them at root.
findings.telemetry: Skill-activation suggestion count for railway-cli/neonctl on prompts containing 'railway deploy' or 'neonctl' (currently structurally 0).

findings.title: Fourth presentation skill family carries ~46MB across 3 overlapping skills, including a bit-identical 6.2MB brand PDF in two skills and a redundant 5.6MB zip of the skill inside itself

evidence.quote: description: Expert guidance for creating Fourth-branded PowerPoint presentations (PPTX files only) using official brand guidelines, templates, colors, typography, and layout principles. Ensures professional, on-brand presentations every time.

description: Generate Fourth-branded EBR/QBR and sales presentations using a two-phase workflow. Phase 1 builds a stunning animated HTML presentation for design review and approval. Phase 2 converts the approved HTML to PPTX for distribution. HTML is always built first -- PPTX is never built until the user explicitly approves the HTML design. Uses the bundled html-engine for visual quality with Fourth brand identity. v6 adds Fourth Midnight palette, 4-color glow rotation, and corrected brand colors.

description: Expert guidance for creating Fourth-branded content across all formats (excluding PowerPoint). Covers brand voice, messaging, visual identity, Fourth iQ branding, tone principles, color systems, typography, and photography for marketing materials, documents, web content, and all communications.

findings.observe_how: du -sk: fourth-presentation-builder 22.8MB, fourth-presentation-suite 12.0MB, fourth-brand-guidelines 11.6MB (~46MB total — by far the heaviest skills in the tree). md5sum confirms 'fourth-presentation-builder/references/Fourth Brand guidelines.pdf' and 'fourth-brand-guidelines/references/Fourth Brand guidelines.pdf' are bit-identical (e1cd86add850965da2c9d40fba80c331, 6,208,470 bytes each). fourth-brand-guidelines additionally stores fourth-brand-guidelines.zip (5,620,402 bytes) — a packaging artifact of itself. Functionally, the suite's two-phase workflow (HTML then PPTX, with its own Fourth_2025_Template.pptx) covers the builder's PPTX-only role, and only the suite is registered in skill-rules.json; the builder (last commit 2026-03-07, referenced only by fourth-brand-guidelines) plus its 2 PPTX/POTX templates duplicates that capability. All ~46MB rides every repo->~/.claude sync and the git history. Simplify: single shared assets/references dir (or keep the PDF in one skill and cross-reference), delete the self-zip, and fold/retire the builder into the suite.
findings.telemetry: Repo size of .claude/skills/ (currently dominated by these 3 dirs); sync-to-active.sh copy volume.

findings.observe_how: Six meta-skills all claim part of the skill-creation lifecycle: skill-developer ('creating and managing'), skill-development ('Skill Development Rules', user-invocable:false), skill-forge (377KB; 'full lifecycle from authoring through validation, testing, optimization, and packaging' — a superset of the other two), skill-upgrader ('Upgrade any skill to v5 Hybrid format', 1 doc ref), vet-skill (external-install vetting, registered), find-skills (discovery, registered). _archived/ even contains archived copies of skill-developer and skill-development while live copies persist — a previous consolidation attempt that didn't finish. Testing cluster: test, full-test-suite (frontmatter says name: full-test, mismatching its full-test-suite directory — whichever identity a router keys on, the other dangles), qa-test, qa-suite, tdd, tdd-migrate (dead, see D7b-04) — overlapping orchestration prose for the same verification job. Consolidation target: skill-forge absorbs skill-developer + skill-upgrader (keep vet-skill and find-skills for their distinct jobs); testing collapses to test + qa-suite (structured) + tdd (philosophy), with full-test-suite either renamed consistently or folded into qa-suite.
findings.telemetry: Per-skill Skill-tool invocation share within each cluster over 30 days — invocation-share <5% for a cluster member supports folding it.

findings.title: Stray ebr-data-prep.skill — a 16KB ZIP archive committed as a flat file in .claude/skills/, never unpacked, not loadable as a skill
findings.observe_how: The file starts with PK zip magic and its central directory lists ebr-data-prep-clean/SKILL.md and ebr-data-prep-clean/scripts/prep_ebr_package.py (16,079 bytes, committed 2026-03-16, b5bffe4). Skills must be <name>/SKILL.md directories — a flat .skill zip is invisible to both the native loader and skill-rules routing, so it is pure junk in the tree and in every sync. Payoff: one `git rm` removes a dead binary from the skill tree and the repo->active sync (or unpack it properly if EBR data prep is still wanted).

findings.title: iq360-event-audit description defers single-query asks to sibling skill `iq360-events` which does not exist in the repo or active ~/.claude/skills

evidence.quote: Differs from `iq360-events`: that skill answers single ad-hoc KQL questions; this skill is for multi-step analyses that end in a report.

findings.observe_how: Grep for 'iq360-events' across .claude/skills finds only iq360-event-audit's own SKILL.md and its evals/trigger_eval.json; `ls .claude/skills | grep iq360` and `ls ~/.claude/skills | grep iq360` both return only iq360-event-audit. The description explicitly instructs the model to 'defer to iq360-events' for single counts/one-liner queries — routing to a skill that doesn't exist, so simple iQ360 queries dead-end or fall back unguided. Payoff: one-line description edit (point at the kusto-cli skill, or restore/create iq360-events) stops the misrouting.
